26.1.m: During the consecrations, he gathers the Mahāvīra pots [materials].

26.1.s: antaḥpātyadeśe sambhārān nidadhāti mṛdaṃ valmīkavapāṃ varāhavihataṃ pūtīkān ajāpayo gavedhukāḥ kṛṣṇājinam abhriṃ cottarataḥ //
26.1.d: अन्तःपात्यदेशे सम्भारान् निदधाति मृदं वल्मीकवपां वराहविहतं पूतीकान् अजापयो गवेधुकाः कृष्णाजिनम् अभ्रिं चोत्तरतः ॥
26.1.m: He deposits the materials in the Antaḥpātya place: clay, an anthill mound, earth dug up by a boar, pūtīka plants, goat milk, gavedhukā grass, a black-antelope skin, and a spade to the north.

26.1.s: devasya tvā \\ ity abhrim ādāyaudumbarīṃ vaikaṅkatīṃ vāratnimātrīm̐ savye kṛtvā dakṣiṇenālabhya japati yuñjate \\ iti //
26.1.d: देवस्य त्वा \\ इत्य् अभ्रिम् आदायौदुम्बरीं वैकङ्कतीं वारत्निमात्रीम्̐ सव्ये कृत्वा दक्षिणेनालभ्य जपति युञ्जते \\ इति ॥
26.1.m: Taking the spade of udumbara or of vikankata wood, a cubit long, with "At the god's [impulsion]...", putting it in his left hand and touching it with his right, he mutters: "They harness...".

26.1.s: mṛdam ādatte piṇḍavat \\ devī dyāvāpṛthivī iti //
26.1.d: मृदम् आदत्ते पिण्डवत् \\ देवी द्यावापृथिवी इति ॥
26.1.m: He takes the clay like a lump with "O divine Heaven and Earth..."
He places it on the black-antelope skin toward the north.
The anthill mound with "O divine ants...".
The earth dug up by a boar with "So large in the beginning...".
The pūtīka plants with "Ye are Indra's strength...".
He touches the collected materials with "For Makha...".

26.1.s: kṛṣṇājinaṃ parigṛhyottarataḥ parivṛtaṃ gachanti praitu brahmaṇaspatir iti //
26.1.d: कृष्णाजिनं परिगृह्योत्तरतः परिवृतं गछन्ति प्रैतु ब्रह्मणस्पतिर् इति ॥
26.1.m: Holding the black-antelope skin, they go to the enclosed space to the north with "May Brahmaṇaspati advance...".
He deposits the materials inside the enclosure.
[The materials are deposited] in the enclosed space with an east-facing door, which has been dug up, sprinkled with water, and strewn with sand, with [the mantra]: "For Makha..."
He mixes [the clay] with the ingredients with [the mantra]: "For Makha..."

26.1.s: mṛdam ādāya makhāya \\ iti mahāvīraṃ karoti prādeśamātram ūrdhvam āsecanavantaṃ mekhalāvantaṃ madhyasaṃgṛhītam ūrdhvaṃ mekhalāyās tryaṅgulam //
26.1.d: मृदम् आदाय मखाय \\ इति महावीरं करोति प्रादेशमात्रम् ऊर्ध्वम् आसेचनवन्तं मेखलावन्तं मध्यसंगृहीतम् ऊर्ध्वं मेखलायास् त्र्यङ्गुलम् ॥
26.1.m: Taking the clay with [the mantra]: "For Makha...", he fashions the Mahāvīra pot, a span in height, provided with a pouring lip, provided with a girdle, constricted in the middle, [and] three finger-breadths [in height] above the girdle.
When it is finished, he touches it with [the mantra]: "The head of Makha..."
In the same manner, [he fashions] the other two [pots], each with its respective mantra.
[He fashions] two milch-pails (pinvana) shaped like the bowl of a sruc ladle, and two round Rauhiṇa-potsherds.
He deposits the reserve clay (upaśayā).
He smooths [them] with Gavedhukā seeds with [the mantra]: "For Makha...", each with its respective mantra.

26.1.s: aśvaśakṛtā dhūpayati \\ aśvasya tvā \\ iti pratimantram //
26.1.d: अश्वशकृता धूपयति \\ अश्वस्य त्वा \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
26.1.m: He fumigates [them] with horse dung with [the mantra]: "The horse's...", each with its respective mantra.

26.1.s: ukhāvad agniḥ pradahanaṃ ca makhāya \\ iti pratimantram //
26.1.d: उखावद् अग्निः प्रदहनं च मखाय \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
26.1.m: The fire and the baking [are performed] like [those of] the Ukhā pot, with [the mantra]: "For Makha...", each with its respective mantra.
He takes them out when baked with [the mantra]: "To the upright one thee...", each with its respective mantra.
He sprinkles [them] with goat's milk with [the mantra]: "For Makha...", each with its respective mantra.
The making, touching, smoothing, fumigating, baking, taking out, and sprinkling of the milch-pails and the rest are done silently.

26.2.m: When about to perform the Upasad rite, one who is to perform [it] performs the Pravargya rite, if [the sacrifice is] accompanied by the Pravargya rite.
The performance of the Pravargya rite takes place with the door closed.
The Parigharmya halter is made of Udumbara wood.
The rope is threefold, made of Muñja grass.
The webbing of the chair made of Udumbara wood, shoulder-high, is of Bālvaja grass.

26.2.s: pūrveṇa gārhapatyaṃ prācaḥ kuśān āstīrya pātrāsādanaṃ dvandvam //
26.2.d: पूर्वेण गार्हपत्यं प्राचः कुशान् आस्तीर्य पात्रासादनं द्वन्द्वम् ॥
26.2.m: Having spread kuśa grass pointing eastward to the east of the Gārhapatya fire, [there is] the setting down of the utensils in pairs:

26.2.s: upayamanīṃ mahāvīram parīśāsau pinvane rauhiṇakapāle rauhiṇahavanyau ca srucāvanutkīrṇe sthūṇāmayūkham dhṛṣṭī śatamāne muñjapralavān vikaṅkataśakalān vim̐śatiṃ prādeśamātrān sruvaṃ muñjavedam dhavitrāṇi paridhīṃś ca rajjusaṃdānam āsandīṃ kṛṣṇājinam abhrim̐ sikatāḥ kharārthā arthavac ca //
26.2.d: उपयमनीं महावीरम् परीशासौ पिन्वने रौहिणकपाले रौहिणहवन्यौ च स्रुचावनुत्कीर्णे स्थूणामयूखम् धृष्टी शतमाने मुञ्जप्रलवान् विकङ्कतशकलान् विम्̐शतिं प्रादेशमात्रान् स्रुवं मुञ्जवेदम् धवित्राणि परिधींश् च रज्जुसंदानम् आसन्दीं कृष्णाजिनम् अभ्रिम्̐ सिकताः खरार्था अर्थवच् च ॥
26.2.m: the supporting shovel (upayamanī), the Mahāvīra pot, the two pairs of tongs, the two milch-pails, the two Rauhiṇa-potsherds, the two Rauhiṇa-offering ladles which are uncarved sruc ladles, the peg-post, the two stirring fire-sticks, the two hundred-māna [pieces of silver and gold], the Muñja-grass tufts, twenty chips of Vikaṅkata wood a span in length, the dipping spoon, the Muñja-grass broom, the fans, the enclosing sticks, the cord-fetters, the chair, the black antelope skin, the spade, sand for the mound, and whatever else is required for the purpose.

26.2.s: prokṣaṇīḥ saṃskṛtyodyamyotthāyāha brahman pracariṣyāmas \\ hotar abhiṣṭuhi \ prastotaḥ sāmāni gāya \\ iti //
26.2.d: प्रोक्षणीः संस्कृत्योद्यम्योत्थायाह ब्रह्मन् प्रचरिष्यामस् \\ होतर् अभिष्टुहि \ प्रस्तोतः सामानि गाय \\ इति ॥
26.2.m: Having prepared the sprinkling waters, lifted [them] up, and stood up, he says: "O Brahman, we shall proceed; Hotṛ, recite the introductory praise; Prastotṛ, sing the Sāmans!"

26.2.s: brahmānujñātas \\ yamāya tvā \\ iti mahāvīraṃ prokṣati //
26.2.d: ब्रह्मानुज्ञातस् \\ यमाय त्वा \\ इति महावीरं प्रोक्षति ॥
26.2.m: Permitted by the Brahman, he sprinkles the Mahāvīra pot with [the mantra]: "For Yama thee..."
Or [he sprinkles it] mantra by mantra, because of the division of sentences.
And [he sprinkles] the Parigharmya halter silently.

26.2.s: pūrvayā dvārā sthūṇāmayūkhaṃ nirhṛtya dakṣiṇato nidhanati hotuḥ saṃdarśane //
26.2.d: पूर्वया द्वारा स्थूणामयूखं निर्हृत्य दक्षिणतो निधनति होतुः संदर्शने ॥
26.2.m: Carrying out the peg-post by the eastern door, he drives it in to the south within the Hotṛ's sight.

26.2.s: gārhapatyāhavanīyā uttareṇa kharau nivapati dakṣiṇato 'nubhitty uchiṣṭakharam //
26.2.d: गार्हपत्याहवनीया उत्तरेण खरौ निवपति दक्षिणतो ऽनुभित्त्य् उछिष्टखरम् ॥
26.2.m: He heaps up two mounds to the north of the Gārhapatya and Āhavanīya fires, [and] the mound for the remnants to the south along the wall.

26.2.s: pūrveṇāhavanīyam̐ samrāḍāsandīṃ paryāhṛtya dakṣiṇataḥ prācīm āsādayati rājāsandyā uttarataḥ kṛṣṇājinam asyām āstṛṇāti tasminn abhryupaśaye nidadhāti mahāvīrau cāvachādayed vā //
26.2.d: पूर्वेणाहवनीयम्̐ सम्राडासन्दीं पर्याहृत्य दक्षिणतः प्राचीम् आसादयति राजासन्द्या उत्तरतः कृष्णाजिनम् अस्याम् आस्तृणाति तस्मिन्न् अभ्र्युपशये निदधाति महावीरौ चावछादयेद् वा ॥
26.2.m: Carrying the emperor's chair (samrāḍ-āsandī) around by the east of the Āhavanīya fire, he sets it down to the south facing east, to the north of the king's chair; on it he spreads the black antelope skin; upon it he places the spade and the reserve clay, and the two [other] Mahāvīra pots, or he should cover [them].
Or another [priest performs] the hitching of the Parigharmya halter, so that the Adhvaryu's time is met.

26.2.s: añjanti \\ ity ucyamāne devas tvā \\ ity anakti mahāvīram ājyam̐ saṃskṛtya //
26.2.d: अञ्जन्ति \\ इत्य् उच्यमाने देवस् त्वा \\ इत्य् अनक्ति महावीरम् आज्यम्̐ संस्कृत्य ॥
26.2.m: While "They anoint..." is being recited, having prepared the clarified butter, he anoints the Mahāvīra pot with [the mantra]: "May the god thee..."

26.2.s: rajataśatamānaṃ khara upagūhati pṛthivyāḥ sam̐spṛśas \\ iti //
26.2.d: रजतशतमानं खर उपगूहति पृथिव्याः सम्̐स्पृशस् \\ इति ॥
26.2.m: He buries the silver hundred-māna piece in the mound with [the mantra]: "From contact with the earth..."

26.3.s: sam̐sīdasva \\ ity ucyamāne muñjapralavān dviguṇān ādīpya pratidiśaṃ khare karoti //
26.3.d: सम्̐सीदस्व \\ इत्य् उच्यमाने मुञ्जप्रलवान् द्विगुणान् आदीप्य प्रतिदिशं खरे करोति ॥
26.3.m: While "Sit down..." is being recited, having ignited the doubled Muñja-grass tufts, he places them in each direction upon the mound.

26.3.s: teṣu mahāvīram ājyavantam arcir asi \\ iti //
26.3.d: तेषु महावीरम् आज्यवन्तम् अर्चिर् असि \\ इति ॥
26.3.m: Upon them [he sets] the Mahāvīra pot filled with clarified butter with [the mantra]: "Thou art the glow..."

26.3.s: anādhṛṣṭā \\ iti vācayati prādeśam adhyadhi dhārayantam //
26.3.d: अनाधृष्टा \\ इति वाचयति प्रादेशम् अध्यधि धारयन्तम् ॥
26.3.m: He makes [the sacrificer] recite [the mantra]: "Unassailable...", while holding his span directly above it.

26.3.s: viśvābhyo mā \\ iti dakṣiṇata uttānaṃ pāṇiṃ nidadhāti //
26.3.d: विश्वाभ्यो मा \\ इति दक्षिणत उत्तानं पाणिं निदधाति ॥
26.3.m: He places his palm turned upward to the south with [the mantra]: "Protect me from all..."
[He places] a span to the north with [the mantra]: "The mares of Manu..."

26.3.s: dhṛṣṭilbhyāṃ bhasmanā parikīryāṅgāraiś ca vikaṅkataśakalaiḥ pariśrayati trayodaśabhiḥ prāgudagbhiḥ svāhā marudbhir iti //
26.3.d: धृष्टिल्भ्यां भस्मना परिकीर्याङ्गारैश् च विकङ्कतशकलैः परिश्रयति त्रयोदशभिः प्रागुदग्भिः स्वाहा मरुद्भिर् इति ॥
26.3.m: Having scattered ash around [the pot] with the two fire-sticks and [having scattered] burning coals, he encloses it with thirteen Vikaṅkata chips pointing eastward and northward, with [the formula]: "Svāhā to the Maruts!"
[He places] an additional one to the south, [and] two with the mantra.
He covers it with the gold hundred-māna piece with [the mantra]: "From contact with the sky..."

26.4.m: And he prompts: "Sing the Candra chant!"

26.4.s: kṛṣṇājināvakṛttair dhavitrair upavājayati tribhir daṇḍavadbhir madhu madhu \\ iti //
26.4.d: कृष्णाजिनावकृत्तैर् धवित्रैर् उपवाजयति त्रिभिर् दण्डवद्भिर् मधु मधु \\ इति ॥
26.4.m: He fans it with three fanning-fans cut from black antelope skin, provided with handles, [whispering]: "Honey! Honey!"

26.4.s: ekaṃ prayachati pratiprasthātre 'param agnīdhe dhūnvantas tristriḥ parikrāmanti pitṛvad devavac ca //
26.4.d: एकं प्रयछति प्रतिप्रस्थात्रे ऽपरम् अग्नीधे धून्वन्तस् त्रिस्त्रिः परिक्रामन्ति पितृवद् देववच् च ॥
26.4.m: He hands one [fan] to the Pratiprasthātṛ, the other to the Agnīdh; fanning, they walk around three times each in the manner of the Pitṛs and in the manner of the gods.

26.4.s: arciṣi prāpte suvarṇaśatamānaṃ nidhāyājyena mahāvīraṃ pariṣiñcati sruveṇa pratipraṇavam //
26.4.d: अर्चिषि प्राप्ते सुवर्णशतमानं निधायाज्येन महावीरं परिषिञ्चति स्रुवेण प्रतिप्रणवम् ॥
26.4.m: When the flame has reached [it], having removed the gold hundred-māna piece, he pours clarified butter around the Mahāvīra pot with the dipping spoon at each praṇava syllable.
He places the two Rauhiṇa cakes on the fire silently, [made] of flour from the village.
They have the properties of clarified butter, because of taking its place.
Or they have the properties of vegetable substances, because of the word denoting their preparation.

26.4.s: īḍe dyāvāpṛthivī ity ucyamāne paridhīn paridhāya rauhiṇā udvāsya srucor āsādayaty āhavanīyād dakṣiṇottarau //
26.4.d: ईडे द्यावापृथिवी इत्य् उच्यमाने परिधीन् परिधाय रौहिणा उद्वास्य स्रुचोर् आसादयत्य् आहवनीयाद् दक्षिणोत्तरौ ॥
26.4.m: While "I praise Heaven and Earth..." is being recited, having laid the enclosing sticks and taken down the two Rauhiṇa cakes, he places them on the two sruc ladles, south and north of the Āhavanīya fire.

26.4.s: apnasvatīm ity ucyamāne rucito gharmas \\ ity āhopottiṣṭhan gharmasya tanvau gāya \\ iti preṣyati //
26.4.d: अप्नस्वतीम् इत्य् उच्यमाने रुचितो घर्मस् \\ इत्य् आहोपोत्तिष्ठन् घर्मस्य तन्वौ गाय \\ इति प्रेष्यति ॥
26.4.m: While "Endowed with wealth..." is being recited, standing up he says: "The Gharma is radiant!", and prompts: "Sing the two bodies of the Gharma!"

26.4.d: परिक्रम्योपतिष्ठन्ते ऽकृतं चेत् \\ गर्भो देवानाम् इति ॥
26.4.m: Having walked around, they stand waiting; if it is not done [yet], with [the mantra]: "The embryo of the gods..."

26.4.s: tvaṣṭṛmantas \\ ity enāṃ vācayati mahāvīram īkṣamāṇām //
26.4.d: त्वष्टृमन्तस् \\ इत्य् एनां वाचयति महावीरम् ईक्षमाणाम् ॥
26.4.m: He makes her recite [the mantra]: "Accompanied by Tvaṣṭṛ...", while looking at the Mahāvīra pot.

26.4.s: ahaḥ ketunā \\ iti dakṣiṇam̐ rauhiṇaṃ juhoti mantrakrameṇottaram \\ rātrir iti sāyam //
26.4.d: अहः केतुना \\ इति दक्षिणम्̐ रौहिणं जुहोति मन्त्रक्रमेणोत्तरम् \\ रात्रिर् इति सायम् ॥
26.4.m: With [the mantra]: "Day with its banner...", he offers the southern Rauhiṇa cake, and the northern one following the order of the mantras; with "Night..." in the evening.

26.5.s: devasya tvā \\ iti rajjusaṃdānam ādāya \\ iḍa ehi \\ iti gām āhvayati nāmnā ca trir uccair apareṇa gārhapatyaṃ gachan //
26.5.d: देवस्य त्वा \\ इति रज्जुसंदानम् आदाय \\ इड एहि \\ इति गाम् आह्वयति नाम्ना च त्रिर् उच्चैर् अपरेण गार्हपत्यं गछन् ॥
26.5.m: Taking the cord-fetters with [the mantra]: "At the impulse of the divine...", he calls the cow with: "Come, O Iḍā!" and by her name three times loudly, going behind the Gārhapatya fire.
He gives the order: "Chant the Dhenu-chant!"

26.5.s: adityai rāsnā \\ iti gāṃ pāśena pratimucya sthūṇāyāṃ baddhvā pūṣāsi \\ iti vatsam utsṛjati //
26.5.d: अदित्यै रास्ना \\ इति गां पाशेन प्रतिमुच्य स्थूणायां बद्ध्वा पूषासि \\ इति वत्सम् उत्सृजति ॥
26.5.m: Fastening the cow with the cord [saying], "Aditi's girdle [thou art]," and tying [her] to the post, he lets loose the calf [saying], "Thou art Pūṣan."

26.5.s: saṃdāya gharmāya dīṣva \\ iti vatsam unnayati //
26.5.d: संदाय घर्माय दीष्व \\ इति वत्सम् उन्नयति ॥
26.5.m: Having tied [her legs], he brings the calf near [saying], "Yield milk for the Gharma offering!"
He milks into the milk-pail [saying], "Swell for the two Aśvins!"
He addresses the drops [saying], "Svāhā, accompanied by Indra!"

26.5.s: yas te stanas \\ iti stanam ālabhate //
26.5.d: यस् ते स्तनस् \\ इति स्तनम् आलभते ॥
26.5.m: He touches a teat [saying], "Which teat of thine..."
In the same manner, the Pratiprasthātṛ [acts with regard to] the she-goat, at a peg, silently.
While "Arise, O Brahmaṇaspati!" is being recited, he stands up.

26.5.s: upadrava payasā \\ ity ucyamāne gachati \\ urv antarikṣam iti //
26.5.d: उपद्रव पयसा \\ इत्य् उच्यमाने गछति \\ उर्व् अन्तरिक्षम् इति ॥
26.5.m: While "Run near with the milk!" is being recited, he goes [saying], "Wide is the intermediate space..."

26.5.s: parīśāsāv ādatte gāyatraṃ chando 'si \\ iti pratimantram //
26.5.d: परीशासाव् आदत्ते गायत्रं छन्दो ऽसि \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
26.5.m: He takes the two pairs of tongs with each respective mantra: "The Gāyatrī metre art thou..."
He gives the order: "Chant the Vasiṣṭhasya śaphau chants!"

26.5.s: tābhyāṃ mahāvīraṃ parigṛhṇāti dyāvāpṛthivībhyāṃ tvā parigṛhṇāmi \\ iti //
26.5.d: ताभ्यां महावीरं परिगृह्णाति द्यावापृथिवीभ्यां त्वा परिगृह्णामि \\ इति ॥
26.5.m: With them he seizes the Mahāvīra pot [saying], "With Heaven and Earth I seize thee."
Having lifted [it], wiped [it] with the broom of muñja-grass, he supports [it] from below with the Upayamanī ladle [saying], "With the intermediate space I hold [thee] from below."

26.5.s: ajāpayasāvasicya śānte goḥ payo 'vanayati \\ indrāśvinā \\ iti //
26.5.d: अजापयसावसिच्य शान्ते गोः पयो ऽवनयति \\ इन्द्राश्विना \\ इति ॥
26.5.m: Having poured goat's milk over [it], when it has quieted down, he pours in the cow's milk [saying], "O Indra and Aśvins!"
While "May Brahmaṇaspati go forth..." is being recited,

26.6.s: samudrāya tvā \\ iti vātanāmāni japati gachann āhavanīyam //
26.6.d: समुद्राय त्वा \\ इति वातनामानि जपति गछन्न् आहवनीयम् ॥
26.6.m: He mutters the names of the wind [saying], "To the ocean thee..." while going to the Āhavanīya fire.
With the Upayamanī ladle he pours [it] out [saying], "Svāhā to the Gharma offering!"

26.6.s: svāhā gharmaḥ pitre \\ iti japitvātikramyāśrāvyāha gharmasya yaja \\ iti //
26.6.d: स्वाहा घर्मः पित्रे \\ इति जपित्वातिक्रम्याश्राव्याह घर्मस्य यज \\ इति ॥
26.6.m: Having muttered "Svāhā, the Gharma offering to the Father!", stepped beyond [the fire], and made the call, he says: "Recite the offering-verse for the Gharma offering!"
When the Vaṣaṭ call has been made, he makes the oblation [saying], "All regions..."
He shakes [the pot] upwards three times [saying], "Bestow [it] in heaven!"
When the secondary Vaṣaṭ call is made, [saying,] "Svāhā to Agni!"
The Brahman follows with a recitation: "O Aśvins, the Gharma offering..."
He addresses [the pot] while it swells [saying], "Swell for food!"
He steps out towards the north-eastern direction [saying], "Thou art the law."
He places [it] upon the mound [saying], "Harmless to us!"

26.6.s: vikaṅkataśakalair juhoti gharme nyajyanyajya svāhā pūṣṇe śarase \\ iti pratimantram //
26.6.d: विकङ्कतशकलैर् जुहोति घर्मे न्यज्यन्यज्य स्वाहा पूष्णे शरसे \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
26.6.m: With chips of vikaṅkata wood, dipping [each] repeatedly into the Gharma offering, he makes oblations, with each respective mantra: "Svāhā to Pūṣan the strong!"
After making each offering, he leans [the chip] against the first enclosing stick.

26.6.s: caturtham ahutam udaṅṅ īkṣamāṇo dakṣiṇato barhiṣy upagūhati //
26.6.d: चतुर्थम् अहुतम् उदङ्ङ् ईक्षमाणो दक्षिणतो बर्हिष्य् उपगूहति ॥
26.6.m: The fourth, without offering, while looking northward, he hides southwards in the sacrificial grass.

26.6.s: saptamaṃ ca sarvalepāktaṃ dakṣiṇekṣamāṇaḥ pratiprasthātre prayachati //
26.6.d: सप्तमं च सर्वलेपाक्तं दक्षिणेक्षमाणः प्रतिप्रस्थात्रे प्रयछति ॥
26.6.m: And the seventh, smeared with all the remnants, he gives to the Pratiprasthātṛ while looking southward.

26.6.s: tam̐ sa uttarataḥ śālāyā udañcaṃ nirasyati //
26.6.d: तम्̐ स उत्तरतः शालाया उदञ्चं निरस्यति ॥
26.6.m: The latter throws it away north of the hall towards the north.

26.6.s: svāhā saṃ jyotiṣā \\ ity upayamanyām āsiñcati gharmyam //
26.6.d: स्वाहा सं ज्योतिषा \\ इत्य् उपयमन्याम् आसिञ्चति घर्म्यम् ॥
26.6.m: He pours out what is in the pot into the Upayamanī ladle [saying], "Svāhā, united with light!"
And he throws the [chips] that were leaned [into the fire].

26.6.s: agnihotrāvṛtā hutvā vājinavad bhakṣayanti madhu hutam iti //
26.6.d: अग्निहोत्रावृता हुत्वा वाजिनवद् भक्षयन्ति मधु हुतम् इति ॥
26.6.m: Having offered in the manner of the Agnihotra, they consume [the remnant] like the Vājina liquid [saying], "The sweet drink is offered..."

26.6.s: ucchiṣṭakhare prakṣālyopayamanīṃ nidadhāty atra vopaśritapraharaṇam̐ sam̐sādyamānāyānuvācayati //
26.6.d: उच्छिष्टखरे प्रक्षाल्योपयमनीं निदधात्य् अत्र वोपश्रितप्रहरणम्̐ सम्̐साद्यमानायानुवाचयति ॥
26.6.m: Having rinsed the Upayamanī ladle on the refuse-mound, he deposits it; or at this moment occurs the throwing in of the leaned [chips]; he causes [the Hotṛ] to recite for the [pots] being placed down.
Some [say the order should be]: "To the ones being placed down..."

26.6.s: sūyavasād bhagavati \\ ity ucyamāne yavasodake dhenave prayachanty eke //
26.6.d: सूयवसाद् भगवति \\ इत्य् उच्यमाने यवसोदके धेनवे प्रयछन्त्य् एके ॥
26.6.m: While "O bountiful one, from the good pasture..." is being recited, some give grass and water to the cow.
He places everything on the chair.
The placing and sprinkling are performed only once for the mounds, posts, pegs, black antelope skin, hoe, Upāśaya pot, and chairs.
Or there is repetition, because they belong to the time of the primary rites.

26.7.m: The disposal of the Pravargya apparatus takes place at the end of the Upasad rites.
Having placed the Parigharmya implements on the Antaḥpātya peg, and having carried the refuse-mound out by the south,

26.7.s: āhavanīye trīñ chālākān pradīpyapradīpyāgnīdhro dhārayati śatarudriyavat pratilomaṃ pramāṇeṣu śatarudriyavat pratilomaṃ pramāṇeṣu //
26.7.d: आहवनीये त्रीञ् छालाकान् प्रदीप्यप्रदीप्याग्नीध्रो धारयति शतरुद्रियवत् प्रतिलोमं प्रमाणेषु शतरुद्रियवत् प्रतिलोमं प्रमाणेषु ॥
26.7.m: Having kindled three firebrands one by one in the Āhavanīya fire, the Agnīdh holds [them], in the manner of the Śatarudriya, in reverse order at the [standard] measures; in the manner of the Śatarudriya, in reverse order at the [standard] measures.

26.7.s: caturgṛhītenābhijuhoti yā te gharma divyā śug iti pratimantram //
26.7.d: चतुर्गृहीतेनाभिजुहोति या ते घर्म दिव्या शुग् इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
26.7.m: He makes an oblation with four ladlings [of butter] with each respective mantra: "Whatever divine heat of thine, O Gharma..."
Having thrown the third [brand into the fire] and sat down,

26.7.s: kṣatrasya tvā \\ iti niṣkramaṇaṃ purastāt patnīm antardhāya //
26.7.d: क्षत्रस्य त्वा \\ इति निष्क्रमणं पुरस्तात् पत्नीम् अन्तर्धाय ॥
26.7.m: The departure takes place from the front with "Thee, of the Kshatriya...", after concealing the wife [from view].
He gives the order for the sāman chant, as at the final bath.
They go to the place of disposal.
Having ordered three times, [the Hotṛ recites] "He has roared..."
He deposits the Pravṛñjanīya pot touching the navel [of the altar], saying: "Four-cornered..."
And the two Rauhiṇa offering ladles, pulled apart, on the outer side.
having placed the grass broom and the cord for tying upon the supporting pan, to the west,
and to the west, the two milking pails on either side of the handle,
the post and peg to the west,
to the south, in the area of the Mārjālīya outside the sacrificial altar, the mound for remnants.

26.7.s: āsecanavanti payasaḥ pūrayati gharmaitat te \\ iti //
26.7.d: आसेचनवन्ति पयसः पूरयति घर्मैतत् ते \\ इति ॥
26.7.m: He fills [the vessels] having pouring-spouts with milk, with the mantra: 'O Gharma, this is yours...!'
He hands over the remainder, mixed with the fast-milk, to the consecrated [sacrificer].
He summons: 'Sing the Vārṣāhara and Iṣṭāhotrīya sāmans!'

26.7.s: cātvāle mārjayante sapatnīkāḥ sumitriyā nas \\ iti //
26.7.d: चात्वाले मार्जयन्ते सपत्नीकाः सुमित्रिया नस् \\ इति ॥
26.7.m: [The priests] along with the [sacrificer's] wife sprinkle themselves at the Cātvāla pit, with the mantra: 'May friendly to us...!'
With the mantra: 'Upwards we [have ascended to the darkness]...', he steps forward towards the north-eastern direction.

26.7.s: anapekṣam etya \\ edho 'si \\ iti samidham ādāyāhavanīye 'bhyādadhāti samid asi \\ iti //
26.7.d: अनपेक्षम् एत्य \\ एधो ऽसि \\ इति समिधम् आदायाहवनीये ऽभ्यादधाति समिद् असि \\ इति ॥
26.7.m: Having returned without looking back, taking a kindling-stick with the mantra: 'You are fuel...', he places it on the Āhavanīya fire with the mantra: 'You are a kindling-stick...'
And the [sacrificer's] wife [places a kindling-stick] on the Gārhapatya fire silently.
He gives the two gold plates of a hundred mānas used in the Pravargya rite to the Brahman priest;
the cow yielding the milk for the Gharma offering to the Adhvaryu priest;
the cow yielding the fast-milk of the sacrificer to the Hotṛ priest;
If the Gharma pot breaks, [the expiation is] as prescribed.

26.7.s: svāhā prāṇebhyaḥ sādhipatikebhyas \\ iti pūrṇāhutim ādyām uttamāṃ ca manasaḥ kāmam ākūtim iti //
26.7.d: स्वाहा प्राणेभ्यः साधिपतिकेभ्यस् \\ इति पूर्णाहुतिम् आद्याम् उत्तमां च मनसः कामम् आकूतिम् इति ॥
26.7.m: With the mantra: 'Svāhā to the vital breaths along with their ruler...', [he offers] the first full-spoon oblation, and the last with: 'The intention and purpose of the mind...'
And [he offers] with the mantra: 'Prajāpati, while being gathered together...', at the proper time;

26.7.d: सविता प्रथमे ऽहन्न् इति च प्रत्यहम् ॥
26.7.m: and on every day, with the mantra: 'Savitṛ on the first day...'
One should perform the Pravargya rite for one who deserves to be seen;
The drawing of the curds-Gharma offering is performed with the mantra: 'As great as Heaven and Earth...!'
The consumption [is performed] with the mantra: 'In me [be placed] that [splendour]...!'
In the Mahāvrata rite, [it is performed] with the mantra: 'The gatherer of splendour...'
The chanting of peace-mantras takes place at the beginning and the end, because of what is seen in the sacred study.
